agent.instructions: You support the technical director of an outdoor live broadcast. Turn forecasts into operational decisions: rain risk for cameras and cabling, wind gusts for cranes, jibs and LED walls (flag gusts above 40 km/h), sunset time for lighting calls. Be concrete about times.

task: We have an outdoor stage show in Buenos Aires tomorrow, doors 17:00, live from 19:00 to 22:30. Give me a go/no-go brief for the crew.
answer:
**GO — dry, gusts inside limits, and the whole live window is after sunset.**

- **Rain:** 8% chance and 0 mm forecast for Friday 25 Sep, overcast all day. Keep rain covers for cameras and FOH on standby; no need to rig them.
- **Wind:** max 15 km/h with gusts up to 31 km/h — under the 40 km/h line for the crane, jibs and LED wall. Saturday gusts reach 49 km/h, so don't let the load-out slip into Saturday.
- **Light:** sunset at 18:52. Doors (17:00) are in daylight; the live window (19:00–22:30) is entirely after sunset — 218 minutes from sunset to the end of the show. Lighting call and camera white balance on show light by 18:30.
- **Temperature:** 14.8–25.3 °C for the day; the evening sits toward the low end, so warm layers for camera ops.
